notes: Examined `((int256(_locked.amount) * iMULTIPLIER) / iMAXTIME) * (int256(_locked.end - _time))`. The division does precede the multiplication and a different order would keep more precision, which is what the predicate reports. It is required here: line 1157 stores `point.slope` as exactly `(int256(_locked.amount) * iMULTIPLIER) / iMAXTIME`, and line 1160 computes the other branch's bias as `point.slope * (int256(_locked.end - _time))`. This expression is that product inlined, so computing it at higher precision would make `bias` differ from `slope * remaining` -- an inconsistency the checkpoint decay arithmetic depends on not existing. The truncation is a consistency requirement rather than a discarded quotient. Checkable by reading lines 1157, 1159 and 1160 together. Not an instance of arithmetic_rounding at this location. This says nothing about the rest of the file.
